QF.id: XIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_64

question.text: What is 'delivery margin' in the context of physical settlement of futures contracts?

answer.text: Additional margin charged on physically-settled futures contracts close to expiry to ensure both parties can fulfill delivery obligations — it is imposed during the delivery period on top of regular margins
The margin refunded when a futures contract is settled by delivery
The standard initial margin that applies throughout the life of the contract
A margin specific to digital delivery of contract notes

explanation.text: The Logic: As physically-settled contracts approach expiry, exchanges impose an additional delivery margin to ensure the long has funds for delivery and the short has securities. This typically starts a few days before expiry and applies in addition to regular margins. Series VIII (p.162) covers stock F&O delivery margins and Series XVI (pp.165-166) covers commodity delivery margins. The Trap: Delivery margin is an additional block of margin near expiry. It is not "refunded" in the ordinary sense — per the source, delivery margins are blocked/collected and then released on completion of settlement or when positions are squared off, subject to obligations and defaults. It applies only to physically-settled contracts. Note: Source-backed by Series VIII p.162 and Series XVI pp.165-166.
